# ECS migration blueprint

**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Status:** execution blueprint, owner decisions recorded 2026-10-10 (§9) · **Law:** `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/*.md`; this document never overrides them, it schedules them.

> **Law 6 — flat archetypes (owner, 2026-10-10, after this blueprint was written).** Every 1-to-1 field lives at the root of the entity and its document; entities are intersections of flat slices (`Appointment = AppointmentMeta & TimeCoordinate & BookingLifecycle & PaymentRecord`); discriminators are domain-prefixed SCREAMING_SNAKE fields (`bookingStatus: 'CONFIRMED'`, `paymentMethod`, `attendanceState`), never `kind`/`type`/`status`; instants are `*UtcMs`, money `*Cents` + `currency`, writes and indexes use root keys. See `CLAUDE.md` Law 6. **The nested component maps, `kind` tags, `*Ms` and `*MinorUnits` names in §2.5–§2.7 and §3 below are pre-Law-6.** They are translated by the **flatten pass**, a step inserted between Phase 3a and the 3b flips (§6): it reshapes every ecs-core component, entity, system, port, spec and shim at once and ships the lint guard, so the 3b flips write flat documents directly. Where this document and Law 6 disagree, Law 6 wins.

> **Law 7 — primitives, shop-anchored time, error structs (owner, 2026-10-10).** No date classes anywhere; the IANA `timeZone` lives only on the shop location — **this supersedes D5's `ZonedInstant { epochMs, zone }` and every per-entity `zone` field below**; every temporal entity carries `localDate: LocalDate` + `MinuteOfDay` fields (all collision, packing, availability and calendar math run on these only) and `utcEpochMs: UtcEpochMs` computed once at ingestion with native `Intl` (indexes, crons, `.ics` only); every coordinate, amount and id is a `Brand<T, B>` primitive from `libs/ecs-core/src/primitives/` with a `Result` smart constructor; errors are flat `{ errorCode: 'BOOKING_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE', … }` structs (replacing `{ code: 'booking.…' }`, i18n keys `errors.<errorCode>`), `throw` only for programmer defects. The flatten pass applies Laws 6 and 7 together. Where this document and Law 7 disagree, Law 7 wins.

**Inputs.** The fourteen verified audit slices (boundaries, domain ×4, application, infrastructure, functions, firestore, web-features ×2, tests, docs, hot-paths), `docs/architecture/module-boundaries.md`, `firestore.indexes.json`, `firestore.rules`, and the files cited below, which were opened wherever two slices disagreed. Every `path:line` below was checked against the tree on 2026-10-10.

**Settled disagreements.** (a) The discriminant is `kind` — settled in the law on 2026-10-10: `.claude/rules/ecs-components.md:61` now states it outright ("The discriminant key is always `kind` — the repo's existing unions and composite indexes (`status.kind`, `effect.kind`) already use it"), and the same day's amendments put the money vocabulary (`*MinorUnits` + `currencyCode`, never `*Cents`, `firestore-layout.md:36`), the `capacity/{YYYY-MM}` paragraph (an owed decision, `firestore-layout.md:67`), the `Map`/`Set` allowance (`ecs-systems.md:60`) and the `CLAUDE.md` §3/§4 kernel-and-owed-decisions text in place, so this document no longer schedules any of them; the example at `.claude/rules/firestore-layout.md:24` already reads `bookingStatus: { kind: 'confirmed', … }` (re-read 2026-10-10, final pass), so nothing about the discriminant is left to amend. (b) Notifications live under `users/{uid}/notifications` (`firestore.rules:163`), not top-level as the layout rule still lists (`firestore-layout.md:61`); the subcollection stays (owner-scoped rules are already right) and the rule text is amended in Phase 1. (c) _withdrawn in round 1_ — `CLAUDE.md:135` and `:143` are not a typo pair: whether the kernel is folded or stays a sibling is the owed decision D3, and `CLAUDE.md:152` forbids pre-empting it; the phase text below is written for both answers and Phase 1 opens with the prerequisite. (d) The Law-2 example stores `timeInterval.endMs` on the appointment (`.claude/rules/ecs-components.md:100`, `.claude/rules/firestore-layout.md:23`) while the scheduling domain insists a seat's end is derived (`libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:102,163,270`); both hold: a seat stores `startMs` only, the appointment's `timeInterval` is the **envelope query key** recomputed by the write plan from the seats, never typed by hand. (e) `InjectionToken` sites: **57 in 50 non-spec files** (grep on 2026-10-10, round 2) — 42 sites in 41 `libs/application/*` port files (the share the migration deletes; two in `libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/schedule-exception-writer.port.ts:79-80` style blocks count once) plus 15 sites in nine Angular-wiring files the blueprint **keeps** under the Law-4 framework exemption of `angular-ui.md`: `libs/infrastructure/firebase-app/src/lib/firebase-app.provider.ts` and `lazy-port.ts` (the `FIREBASE_*` tokens and `provideLazyPort`, §4.3/§5.3), `libs/infrastructure/storage/src/lib/storage.provider.ts`, `libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/code-scanner/code-scanner.ts`, `libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/camera/camera-media.ts`, `libs/ui/controls/src/lib/map/maplibre-loader.ts`, `libs/ui/icons/src/lib/registry/icon-registry.service.ts`, `libs/features/client/onboarding/src/lib/services-cap.ts`, `libs/features/shared/visits/src/lib/testing/visit-fixtures.ts`. The lint selector of §6 Phase 1 is therefore suffix-scoped, never "everywhere except one file".

## 1. Findings — the repo today

### 1.1 Project inventory (62 Nx projects, 56 `@creativo/*` aliases)

Toolchain: Nx 23.1, Angular 22.2, TypeScript 6.0.3, pnpm. Two tsconfig chains — chain A (`module: commonjs`, node resolution) for `libs/domain/*`, `libs/application/*`, `libs/ui/tokens`; chain B (`module: preserve`, decorators) for every Angular lib and `apps/web`. `apps/functions` builds with esbuild (`cjs`, `bundle: false`, `generatePackageJson`) and therefore ships `@angular/core`, `@angular/compiler` and `rxjs` to Cloud Functions because thirty compiled port files `require('@angular/core')` for their `InjectionToken` (e.g. `libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/availability-reader.port.ts:1,73`).

**Out of scope — design only.** The docs slice lists designs with no code behind them: the capability layer (`CapabilitySystem`), adjustments / approvals / held notifications, client merge, claims and erasure (P5), slot holds, the BarberDay private ledger with period roll-ups and sealing, `bookingCommits`, `settings/{supportPolicy,loyaltyPolicy}`, points expiry and opening balances, rule-change notice, holds TTL. None of them gets an entity, a collection or a reserved field in this blueprint; they are parameterised later on top of the archetypes below (§9 D26, with their design docs named there).

---

## 2. Domain map → archetypes

Naming: entities `*.entity.ts` under `libs/ecs-core/src/entities/`, components `*.data.ts` under `components/`, systems `*.system.ts` under `systems/`, port types under `ports/`. An entity is `{ id, …components }`; a component is a plain readonly struct with an `as const` companion and a type-only namespace; a system is a module of pure functions taking `nowMs`/`nextId` as arguments.

`weekday` is ISO 1..7, computed **once per row** inside `dayTable` from the civil epoch day as `((epochDay + 3) % 7 + 7) % 7 + 1` — the pure `isoWeekdayOf` already at `recurrence-rule.ts:104-106` — because every table consumer keys on a weekday: `shopDayHours` indexes opening hours by `day.weekday()` (`roster-window.ts:58-59`), `ShiftSegment.weekday`, the location's seven `DayHours` (indexed by weekday), RecurrenceSystem's weekly/monthly patterns and the month grid, and `new Date(...).getUTCDay()` is lint-banned in `*.system.ts`); `dayKeyOf`, `minuteOfDay`, `instantOf`, `startOfDayMs`, `addDays` are subtraction and binary search over a table passed in; `instantOf(day, wallMinutes)` and `minuteOfDay(ms, day)` are the **two-branch** subtraction over the transition fields (before `transitionAtMinutes`: `dayStartMs + wallMinutes·60 000`; at or after it: the same minus `transitionDeltaMinutes·60 000`, a wall minute inside the erased segment resolving forward), so a post-switch shift is never an hour off; `dayTable`/`dayTableAround` are the only functions that fill those fields. Roster/Busy/Capacity/GridLayout/ShopClock/CalendarGrid/Recurrence take the table as a parameter and never call `Intl` or construct a `Date`; the pipeline or store builds it once per request / visible range |

### 2.6 Entity catalogue

Each shape is written **once**, here; §3.1 references these rows and adds nothing to the body. Every row is derived from the cited `*-document.ts` / adapter writer as "stored body minus the id field, ISO → `*Ms`, `Record` → array, `'HH:mm'` → minutes, nothing else" — any other change (a nesting such as `baseTerms` or a nested `Money`, a rename such as `hours` → `openingHours`, a new field such as `users.registration` or `clientJournal.appointmentId`, a dropped duplicate) is **declared in its row by name**, and repeated in the §3.1 target cell; a field a row does not name is not stored. Absent is `null`, never `?` (hidden-class rule, §6 Phase 1 lint). TTL `purgeAt` Timestamps are **not** entity fields: the adapter stamps them at the document root on write and **drops them on read** — `const { purgeAt: _, ...body } = snap.data(); return { id, ...body }` (§3.5) — for **type honesty only**: the value the adapter returns is then exactly the entity type, with no field the type does not declare. The destructure does **not** make loaded and system-built entities share one hidden class, and nothing here claims it: `snap.data()` builds the object by iterating the proto's `Object.keys(fields)` (`@google-cloud/firestore/build/src/document.js:342`), i.e. in Firestore's key order, not the declaration order a write-plan literal uses, and two objects with the same keys inserted in a different order have different V8 maps. **Load-boundary polymorphism is accepted:** a loaded entity and a built one may differ in map; the hot loops of §2.8 (the availability DFS, the busy and capacity merges, the grid sweep) run over arrays that the system itself builds from those entities — `MinuteBlock[]`, `CapacityEntry[]`, index arrays — so the inner loops stay monomorphic whatever the load order was. The one destructure in the adapter is not a mapper, it is the read half of the stamp.

### 2.8 System catalogue

All signatures are pure; `nowMs`, `nextId`, `hash`, budgets and caps are parameters; inputs are readonly arrays scanned linearly; every system ships a purity spec (same inputs → deep-equal outputs, no `Date`/`Math.random`/`crypto` reachable — `node:crypto` is lint-banned in `*.system.ts`, §6 Phase 1). Zone math takes a `readonly DayOffset[]` table (§2.5) and never calls `Intl` — only `ZonedTimeSystem` does, through its per-zone formatter cache (§9 D5: native `Intl`, no Luxon). Snapshots reach the engines already partitioned per shop by the loader (hot-paths Q4), so no system sees cross-shop geometry. Systems return numbers, ids and tags; words, currency strings and Roman numerals are made in the template layer (`angular-ui.md`).

budget respected; **hot path #1 is committed to a sorted-struct, index-addressed layout, written here so the port cannot be naïve:** (1) barbers and lines are index arrays — `q.barbers: readonly BarberDayAvailability[]`, `q.lines: readonly AvailabilityLine[]`, and the DFS compares **indexes**, never id strings; (2) `AvailabilityLine.termsByBarber: readonly LineTerms[]` is a dense array parallel to `q.barbers` (one entry per barber, the line's default terms repeated where no override exists) replacing today's optional `ReadonlyMap<string, LineTerms>` (`availability.ts:39,60`) and the `termsForBarber` lookup; (3) `blocks`, `release` and `personKey` are **required** (`[]` / `[]` / `null`), so the three shape-toggling optionals of `availability.ts:39,98,136` are gone and every node sees one hidden class; (4) eligible barbers are precomputed once per line as `readonly number[]` index lists before the search (today `eligible()` re-filters all barbers per branch, `:350-356`); (5) the chosen assignments live in a preallocated per-barber **taken stack** (push on descent, pop on return) with a parallel per-line cursor array, so no branch runs `chosen.filter().map()`/`chosen.some()` (`:483,495-507,518,550`); (6) candidate starts are iterated **inline** over the already-sorted free gaps (`for gap… for start…`) — `candidateStarts` no longer materialises a `number[]` per (line, barber) per branch (`:226-249`); (7) `isTighter` compares `envelope.endMs` then the barber **index** sequence element by element — no `map().join()` string keys (`:338-348`); (8) `AvailabilityOption` is built only when a leaf is accepted; (9) `AvailabilityQuery` keeps **every** field present too — today it has three more optionals (`maxOptions?` :199, `riders?` :205, `withinMs?` :215): `withinMs: readonly TimeInterval[] \| null`, where `null` is unconstrained and `[]` is "nothing qualifies" (the source's own warning, `availability.ts:207-214`), with one spec case each, so a porter who maps the optional to `[]` fails a test instead of returning zero availability for every ordinary booking; `riders: readonly AvailabilityRider[]`, `[]` on every ordinary booking (only a client move carries riders); `maxOptions` leaves the query and joins `nodeBudget` in `SearchBudget`. ## 3. Firestore target layout

Law 5 (`.claude/rules/firestore-layout.md`): the document body is the entity minus its id; instants are epoch ms (`*Ms`), in-day times are minutes-of-day, money is `*MinorUnits` + `currencyCode`; no dynamic-key maps; arrays that are never queried get a `fieldOverrides` entry; a composite index is declared beside the query that needs it; appointments are callable-only.

### 3.5 TTL, rules, projections

- **TTL** (never enabled today): exactly the five `purgeAt` fields `.claude/rules/firestore-layout.md` names, with their existing offsets kept — `otps.purgeAt` (= expiry + 24 h, `firestore-otp-repository.ts:30-31`), `notifications.purgeAt` (= `sentAt` + 90 d, `firestore-notification-writer.ts:39`), `waitlistRequests.purgeAt` (= last day + 7 d), `barberBusy.purgeAt` (= day + 30 d, `rebuild-busy.ts:116`), `capacity.purgeAt` (= month-end + 40 d, `rebuild-capacity.ts:333`) — plus `impersonationSessions.purgeAt` (= `expiresAtMs` + 30 d, stamped at `startImpersonation`, re-stamped = `endedAtMs` + 30 d at `endImpersonation`, so a session that lapses without an end call still ages out) and `barberLeadTimeSamples.purgeAt` (§3.1), so no collection has two spellings of one instant. TTL fields are Firestore `Timestamp`s because the TTL service requires it; they are **adapter-stamped root fields outside the entity type** (the adapter adds them on write; `{ id, ...data }` carries them harmlessly; the entity keeps `expiresAtMs`/`endedAtMs` for math), named without the `Ms` suffix. `firestore-layout.md` is amended in Phase 1 with this Timestamp-not-ms exception and its TTL sentence (`:67`, five groups today) is **extended to the seven** collection groups named here — `otps`, `notifications`, `waitlistRequests`, `barberBusy`, `capacity`, `impersonationSessions`, `barberLeadTimeSamples` — so the rule and the Phase 3 runbook list the same seven; the list is extended, never shrunk.
- **Cloud Storage:** `storage.rules` is unchanged by the migration. Its three prefixes — `avatars/{userId}/{fileName}` (owner-written, world-readable, `storage.rules:38-45`), `media/**` (public catalog media, written only by admin tooling, `:51-54`) and `appointmentPhotos/{appointmentId}/{photoId}` (staff-only both ways, `:61-`) — are what `AppointmentPhotoEntity.path`, `MediaRef.path` and the media ports of §4.2 (`UploadAvatar`/`FindAvatar`/`RemoveAvatar`, `ResolveMedia`, `UploadPhotoBytes`) address; the Firestore reshaping moves no object and renames no prefix.

### 3.6 Notes

- **Epoch ms vs ISO.** Eight composites order on ISO strings today (§3.3): #6, #10 (`createdAt`), #15, #17, #18, #19, #20 (`at`) and #22. ISO orders correctly only within one offset; the moment a stamp is written in a different zone (`appointment-seed-document.ts:62-96` hand-builds canonical ISO for exactly this reason) ordering breaks silently. Epoch ms orders globally, costs no parse on the hot paths (#6 rebuild-busy, #3 grid), and keeps `zone` as a separate string so day keys stay recoverable. There is no backfill and no dual-shape reader: CLAUDE.md §0 owes no backward compatibility ("No production users, no backward compatibility, no schema deprecation duty") and Law 5 forbids a `startMs ?? Date.parse(startIso)` fallback as a mapper in the adapter. Phase 3b ships the new document shapes, rules and indexes in **vertical flips cut along read/write closures** — a flip is the set of collections whose readers and writers share code (the reader matrix of §6 Phase 3b), and it carries every pipeline, server adapter, `lib/**` handler, web `*.adapter.ts` bundle, store field, seed path, rules line, index and fixture that reads **or** writes any of them — so **every reader of a collection matches its shape at every commit** (a flip cut per collection alone would leave, e.g., `FirestoreBookingStore.load` parsing `hours`/`timezone` after the catalog reshaped and /book showing every shop closed); the emulator and any dev project are wiped and reseeded (`pnpm run seed:dev`); the adapter does `{ id, ...snap.data() }` and nothing else. A one-off conversion script under `tools/seed` exists only if the owner names a dataset worth keeping (§6 Phase 3).
- **`capacity/{YYYY-MM}` days map.** It is the one knowingly violated Law-5 spot (`CLAUDE.md:150`). Today's write (`rebuild-capacity.ts:322-351`) is **not** a whole-document rewrite: it `tx.set`s a seed only when the month doc is absent (:326-334) and otherwise `tx.update(monthRef, new FieldPath('days', dayKey, barberId), contribution | FieldValue.delete())` scoped to ONE barber's days — a per-path replace, which is exactly the invariant the layout rule protects (`set({ merge: true })` cannot delete a shop key that filled up). The `entries[]` target must state the same invariant or it regresses: inside the rebuild transaction read the month doc, merge the plan's sorted entries into the month's sorted `entries[]` in one linear pass that skips every existing entry whose `(barberId, dayKey)` is in the plan's scope (a two-pointer merge — no append-then-sort), write the **full sorted array** — never `arrayUnion`, never a merge, never a rewrite from one barber's plan alone (that deletes other barbers' entries) — and re-assert it in `rebuild-capacity.integration.spec.ts` (the replace-not-merge oracle, tests Q0). `CapacitySystem.applyPlan` is that fold (§2.8). Recommended target: the sorted `entries[]` array (one document, one read, linear scan of ≤ 31 × barbers × shops rows, fieldOverride on `entries`); the per-day sub-document alternative costs up to 31 reads per month view.

## 4. Ports, pipelines, adapters

Law 4: a pipeline is `(ports) => async (cmd) => Result`, read → pure system → write; server pipelines live in `apps/functions/src/pipelines/*.pipeline.ts`, beside their composition root, and browser command pipelines beside the feature store that uses them — never in ecs-core, which has no `pipelines/` folder (§9 D27(b)); ports are function types in `libs/ecs-core/src/ports/`; adapters are plain `(db) => port` functions in `apps/functions/src/adapters/*.adapter.ts` (server) and `libs/infrastructure/firestore/src/lib/*.adapter.ts` (browser); the Firestore transaction is the sandwich; `InjectionToken` meets ecs-core in exactly one file, `libs/infrastructure/firebase-app/src/lib/ports.tokens.ts` (Angular wiring; `app.config.ts` only consumes those constants) — the nine Angular-wiring files of settled disagreement (e) keep their own tokens under the Law-4 framework exemption, and the lint selector of §6 Phase 1 and Risk 6 are scoped to the ECS suffixes and `apps/functions/**`, never to the whole repo. Every transactional pipeline is read → decide → **one** write plan (`readonly writes: WriteOp[]`, `WriteKind = { Set, Create, Update, Delete }` as const — both declared in `components/write-op.data.ts`, §2.7, so systems can return them) committed by the single `CommitPlan` port of `tx.port.ts`: the pipeline's read callback receives a `ReadTx = { get, getAll, query }` and **nothing that writes**, and `set`/`create`/`update`/`delete` exist only inside the adapter that applies the returned `WriteOp[]` (`ecs-pipelines.md`'s `read: (tx: ReadTx) => …` / `writes: WriteOp[]` shape); voucher restores, busy merges and waitlist notifications are entries in that plan, never a second write port. The two sanctioned writes **after** a commit are `enqueue` (tasks) and `appendAudit` — `AppendAudit = (rows: readonly AuditEntryEntity[]) => Promise<void>` in `governance.port.ts`: rows planned by `AuditSystem.plan`, ids `hash(AuditSystem.rowBasis(…))`, each written with `create()` (ALREADY_EXISTS is the replay, not an error), **never fatal** (a failure is logged through `Log`/`TrackError`, the booking stands) — today's `appendAudit` contract (`apps/functions/src/lib/booking/audit.ts:286`, "after the commit, never inside it", `transition-appointment.ts:494`). The one audit row written **inside** a transaction is `publishStreakDefinition`'s, as today (`firestore-streak-definition-store.ts:44,143,224`).

what serializes them is Auth's uniqueness of phone and email — the loser's `createUser` fails with `auth/phone-number-already-exists` / `auth/email-already-exists` (today surfaced as `TokenMintingFailure`, `verify-otp.use-case.ts:213-217`). On that refusal the pipeline resolves the winner's uid through an added `findAuthUserByDestination` port (`auth.getUserByPhoneNumber` / `getUserByEmail` in the same Admin-Auth adapter) — not the users query alone, which can return `null` in the window where the winner's Auth user exists but its stub does not — and signs in to it, writing or keeping the stub. The stub is written with `create()`, ALREADY_EXISTS treated as success: its purpose is narrower than the race — a retried stub write can never clobber a body `completeRegistration` already wrote. Emulator spec: two concurrent first verifications of one phone → one Auth user, one stub, both sign in to the same uid; `OtpCrypto.hashCode` (same bundle) computes the `codeMatches` boolean `OtpSystem.verify` takes. **Auth failures keep today's wire:** a `PipelineError` from `mintCustomToken`, `provisionAuthUser` or `findAuthUserByDestination` is answered as `token_minting_failure` (`LegacyWireCode.TokenMintingFailure`: `internal`, `{ code, params: {} }`, pinned in `edge.spec.ts`) — never the raw `pipeline.unknown` / `pipeline.unavailable`, which no i18n key words | OtpSystem, RegistrationSystem                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `otpId` + `attempts` CAS; Auth's unique phone/email for the first-verification race; the stub's `create()` (ALREADY_EXISTS = success)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

It is created in Phase 1; each 3b flip deletes its collections' duplicate constants — `libs/infrastructure/firestore/src/lib/firestore-paths.ts:64-156`, the application `*_COLLECTION` exports (`AUDIT_LOG_COLLECTION`, `CLIENT_STATS_COLLECTION`, …), the functions copies and the seed literals — so the 23 constants across 12 modules of §1.2 L5 end at one.

### 4.3 Composition root, telemetry

- **Server root:** `apps/functions/src/main.ts` becomes the only place that constructs ports: `const db = getFirestore(); const ports = firestorePorts(db, { nowMs: () => Date.now(), nextId: randomUUID, hash: sha256Hex })` (`hash` from `adapters/crypto.adapter.ts`, the only `node:crypto` import), then one `onCall`/`onDocumentWritten`/`onSchedule` per pipeline, each handler being `edge(pipeline(ports))` where `edge` maps `Result` errors to `HttpsError` (the 81 inline throws collapse to one table) and attaches `work-budget`; an availability refusal carries the public `barberBusy` day body in `HttpsError.details` (docs Q4 — it is world-readable anyway, so the client re-renders without a second read). Handlers hold no logic.
- **Web root:** `app.config.ts` keeps `provideFirestoreDb`, `FIREBASE_*`, `provideLazyPort` but binds **port bundles** — plain objects of function members, never a bare function token, because `lazyPort` proxies named `methods` with `Reflect.apply` and cannot proxy a bare function (§5.3): `{ provide: SCHEDULING_READ_PORTS, useFactory: () => schedulingReadPorts(inject(FIRESTORE)) }` for an eager bundle, and `provideLazyPort(SCHEDULING_READ_PORTS, scope, { factory: m => (inj) => m.schedulingReadPorts(inj.get(FIRESTORE)), methods: { observeBusyDay: 'observable', observeSchedule: 'observable', observeExceptions: 'observable', observeLocation: 'observable', observePolicy: 'observable' } })` for a lazy one — the same `(db) => bundle` export as the eager form, picked through the §5.3 `factory` member — with the `methods` map of §5.3; the 9 `useClass` rows go, the 31 lazy bindings stay lazy (chunking is a bundle-budget concern, `verify:bundle`).
- **Pino / Sentry:** not installed. `ports/telemetry.port.ts` declares the law's signatures **verbatim** (`.claude/rules/ecs-pipelines.md`): `Log = (level: 'info' | 'warn' | 'error', msg: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) => void` and `TrackError = (error: unknown, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void` — so a pipeline calls `ports.log('warn', 'booking.rejected', { code })` as the rule's example does, no `LogEvent`/`ErrorContext` struct is invented, and no rule amendment is owed (the optional `fields?`/`context?` are function **parameters**, which the optional-property guard of §6 Phase 1 leaves legal); `apps/functions/src/adapters/console-telemetry.adapter.ts` wraps `firebase-functions/logger` (the 19 existing sites) today, `pino-telemetry.adapter.ts` + `sentry-telemetry.adapter.ts` are added when the packages are (CLAUDE.md:150). Telemetry is invoked only in `edge()` and in the write half; systems never log.
- **Hono `apps/api` question (stated neutrally).** For: one HTTP surface, local dev without the Functions emulator, Cloud Run concurrency, no `firebase-functions` coupling in handlers. Against: 11 Firestore triggers and 3 schedules have no Hono equivalent and would still need Functions or Eventarc; `verify:p0` and the emulator suite (`package.json:12`) are built around `firebase emulators:exec`; `hono` is not a direct dependency; the migration already touches every handler. **Recommendation:** stay on Cloud Functions v2 for this migration; make `main.ts` the root so that a later `apps/api` is a second root over the same `ports` object with zero pipeline changes. No Hono code in this blueprint.

### 5.2 Deleted on the web side

- Mappers: `appointment-document.ts`, `loyalty-document.ts` (+ `FieldReader`), `client-stats-document.ts` and the other 44 mapper functions in `libs/infrastructure/firestore` — the document IS the entity body (§3).
- The 35 `new XxxUseCase(…)` sites in client features and the 37 `*UseCase` classes; a component calls a pipeline function or reads an entity signal.
- `translateDomainError` keeps its 125 bg/en keys but takes `{ code }` structs; the 9 feature files passing `DomainError` instances change one import each.
- `libs/application/*` ports with `InjectionToken` (42 sites); the token constants that Angular still needs are re-declared in `libs/infrastructure/firebase-app/src/lib/ports.tokens.ts` as `InjectionToken<PortBundle>` — the plain object of function members `.claude/rules/ecs-pipelines.md` prescribes (`SchedulingReadPorts = { observeBusyDay: …; observeSchedule: …; observeExceptions: …; observeLocation: …; observePolicy: … }` — raw entity streams; availability is derived in the store, §4.2), never a bare function type — the only file where `InjectionToken` and ecs-core meet.

### 5.3 `app.config.ts` wiring (532 lines today)

Keep `provideFirestoreDb` (`firestore-db.provider.ts:20`), `FIREBASE_*` tokens, `provideLazyPort`/`LazyAdapterScope`, `subscribeWithRetry`, `retryDelayMs`. The real seam (`lazy-port.ts:122,160,205,403,461`) is `provideLazyPort(token, scope, { adapter: Picker<M, P>, methods: { name: 'observable' | 'promise' }, onLoadError })` where `Picker<M, P> = (module: M) => Type<P>`, `LazyAdapterHost.adapter(type)` does `injector.get(type)` (classes only) and `lazyPort` returns `Object.fromEntries` of the named methods forwarded with `Reflect.apply` — a bare function-typed token cannot be proxied by it. So: (1) tokens bind port **bundles** (`InjectionToken<SchedulingReadPorts>`, §5.2), which keeps the `methods` classification and `onLoadError` working unchanged; (2) **before any web adapter is rewritten** (the first item of Phase 3b, §6), the seam becomes **two-form** for the duration of 3b, specified in full against the real seam (`lazy-port.ts:179-272`) — flip (0) cannot simply replace `Picker` with a factory, because the 31 `provideLazyPort` rows (`adapter: (m) => m.firestore.FirestoreAppointmentRepository`, `app.config.ts:280`, …) return class constructors, which do not satisfy a call signature, so `app.config.ts` would not typecheck until the last flip: `provideLazyPort` keeps `adapter: Picker<M, P>` (`(module: M) => Type<P>`, the class form and its child-injector path) **beside** a new `factory: FactoryPicker<M, P>` member (`(module: M) => (injector: EnvironmentInjector) => P`), exactly one of the two per row; `LoadedScope` keeps its `Map<Type, EnvironmentInjector>` (one child `createEnvironmentInjector([type], …)` per class, destroyed on a throw) for the class rows **and** adds a `Map<factory, P>` that creates each bundle once as `runInInjectionContext(scopeInjector, () => factory(scopeInjector))` — a factory called as a plain `(injector) => P` outside an injection context would throw NG0203 the moment it used `inject()` — dropping the cache entry when the factory throws, so the next call retries; `LazyAdapterHost.adapter` keys `failing`/`report` by the **factory** and names it by `factory.name` (today by the `Type`, `:252-272`); `methods` and `onLoadError` unchanged. Each flip moves its rows from `adapter` to `factory`; **the last flip** deletes the class form, `Picker` and the `Map<Type, EnvironmentInjector>`. Lazy rows read `factory: m => (inj) => m.schedulingReadPorts(inj.get(FIRESTORE))`, which matches the eager `(db) => bundle` export of §4.3. The wiring spec covers **both forms** while both exist — create-once, throw-then-retry, destroy, and an NG0203 regression case for the factory form, its existing cases for the class form; (3) the 9 `useClass` and the 31 `provideLazyPort(TOKEN, scope, { adapter: m => m.SomeAdapterClass, … })` rows become `{ factory: m => (inj) => m.schedulingReadPorts(inj.get(FIRESTORE)), methods: { observeBusyDay: 'observable', … } }`, each in its collection's flip. Feature stores inject the same tokens; a bundle member is called where a method was.

## 6. Phase plan

Each phase ends green on `pnpm nx run-many -t typecheck`, `pnpm nx run-many -t test`, `pnpm nx run-many -t lint`, `pnpm nx build web`, `pnpm nx build functions` (`CLAUDE.md:158-162`), plus the phase gate named below. Nothing is deleted before its replacement is wired; the app runs at every phase boundary.

### Phase 1 — Foundation (ecs-core, lint, kernel)

**Prerequisites: D2, D3, D4, D5, D7, D8, D10, D13, D15, D16, D17, D18, D19, D20, D21, D22, D23, D24, D25 and D28 — confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-10 (§9), D5 amended to native `Intl` and D4 to no dinero.js; Phase 1 may start** (`CLAUDE.md` §4 — "do not reopen a decided question in code"). DST divergences from the legacy class, intended (recorded 2026-10-10 after a scratch comparison against the Luxon-backed kernel): the legacy `ZonedDateTime.fromParts` probed for a repeated wall time at +1 h, and when it ran in winter it silently resolved a repeated time (Sofia 2026-10-25 03:30 in `reject` mode) to its SECOND occurrence instead of failing. It also never saw Australia/Lord_Howe's 30-minute overlap, and its `startOf('day')` took the second of two midnights (America/Scoresbysund 2018-10-28). `ZonedTimeSystem` rejects the first two unless the caller names a `DstResolution`, and starts the day at the first midnight. The rejection is intended, and `zoned-time.system.spec.ts` pins all three.

### Phase 3 — Pipelines, adapters, API, Firestore reshaping

**Prerequisites: D1, D9, D11, D12, D14, D27 and the two remaining halves of D28 (coupon admin writes; the `verifyOtp` payload) — confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-10 together with the Phase 1 set (D7, D8, D15–D17, D20, D23, D24 and D28's other halves), §9, with D12 and D27 resolved as (b).** Phase 3 opens with **no** law amendment: under D27(b) the pipelines live in `apps/functions/src/pipelines/`, and the `CLAUDE.md` §3 / `AGENTS.md` text saying so (and that ecs-core has no `pipelines/` folder) already landed on 2026-10-10. D11 is here because this phase writes `console-telemetry.adapter.ts` (D11(a)). The file list below implements D1(a) (`apps/functions/src/edge.ts`, `main.ts` as the only root), D27(b) (pipelines under `apps/functions/src/pipelines/`), D7 (capacity `entries[]`), D8(a) (the twelve models importers move to the ecs-core brands in the identity flip — **the D8(b) delta:** they stay on `libs/domain/models`, which re-exports the ecs-core brands, and the flip replaces only the class ids), D9(b) (**no** `save-program-content` pipeline: `AdminProgramsStore` keeps its rules-guarded admin write, re-typed to the §2.6 bodies in the programs flip — the D9(a) delta is in Create below), D12(b) (**no** contact-change pipelines), D11(a) (console telemetry), D15, D16(b) (no `scheduleExceptionNotes` collection), D17 (`{ seconds, nanos }`), D20, D23 and D24 — so under any other answer the phase is re-cut, never pre-empted (`CLAUDE.md:152`). **The D1(b) delta, so choosing (b) does not invalidate the phase:** an `apps/api` project (`scope:backend`, `type:app`, chain A, Hono on Cloud Run) whose `routes/*.router.ts` is a **second root over the same `firestorePorts(db, …)`** assembler; the 15 callables (`requestOtpChallenge`, `verifyOtpChallenge`, `completeRegistration`, `commitBooking`, `cancelAppointment`, `rescheduleAppointment`, `transitionAppointment`, `markArrived`, `clearArrival`, `recordSeatTip`, `staffEditAppointment`, `requestWaitlist`, `cancelWaitlist`, `publishStreakDefinition`, `runBackfill` — plus the new ones) move to typed Hono RPC routes and the SPA's `callableClient` (§4.2) targets them by base URL from the environment instead of `httpsCallable`, keeping the one error translation; the 11 triggers and 3 schedules stay in `main.ts`; `verify:p0` and `e2e:web` gain a local Cloud Run process (`pnpm nx serve api`) started beside `firebase emulators:exec`, and `pnpm run test:emulator` keeps the Functions emulator for the triggers. The pipelines and adapters list is unchanged either way.

**The flatten pass (Law 6, inserted 2026-10-10) runs between 3a and the first 3b flip**: one change reshapes every ecs-core slice and entity to the flat form, renames discriminators, instants and money fields, updates the Phase 2 systems, specs, shims and test doubles, and lands the lint guard (no `kind`/`type`/`status` property names and no nested 1-to-1 object literals in `*.data.ts`/`*.entity.ts`); it is gated like a phase. Every flip below then writes the flat bodies.

**Phase 3 is 3a, then 3b as a sequence of per-collection vertical flips — no mapper bridge.** (Final-pass choice between the two options the review offered: option (b), letting 3a's new adapters call the `libs/application` mappers as a temporary exception, would bend Law 5 and needs the owner's sign-off, so the blueprint is written for option (a); if the owner prefers (b) the content of the flips is unchanged and only their grouping is.) The 3a/3b split of the earlier rounds could not be built: 3a's new adapters were to run pipelines over `AppointmentEntity` (ms, `bookingStatus`, `timeInterval`) while still writing today's `startIso`/`status`/`byVariant`, and the only code converting between the two is the legacy mapper set of `@creativo/application/booking` (`appointmentFromDocument`/`appointmentToDocument`, imported at `apps/functions/src/adapters/firestore-booking-store.ts:18-31`) — a `functions → libs/application` edge the 3a gate banned, or a new ISO↔ms mapper in an adapter that Law 5 bans. **3a** = everything that does not depend on a document body (no law amendment opens it — under D27(b) the `CLAUDE.md` text already landed): `edge.ts`, the `main.ts` composition root (each export still delegates to today's `lib/**` handler until its collection flips, so names, ids and shapes are untouched), the body-free adapters (`crypto`, `otp-crypto`, `console-otp-sender`, `console-telemetry`, `auth-claims`, the `CommitPlan`/`ReadTx` adapter and the `firestorePorts` assembler skeleton — the legacy classes they succeed stay until their last importer goes, Deletions below), the `seed-tools` retag (below), the reader matrix and the ecs-core test doubles the later flips need. **3a lands no pipeline over a reshaped collection** — every collection of the list below changes its body, so every pipeline arrives with its collection's flip. **3b** = the vertical flips, one commit each. **A flip is the read/write closure of its collections, not one collection.** Ordering flips by which code _writes_ a collection, as the earlier rounds did, leaves code that only _reads_ it on the old shape: a flip reshaping `locations` and `services` alone would leave `FirestoreBookingStore.load` (`toShop` reads `data['hours']`/`data['timezone']`, `toService` the root `priceMinorUnits`, `firestore-booking-store.ts:644-666`; `toSchedule` the `weeklyPattern`, `:690-731`; `exceptionFromDocument`, `:510`), `rebuild-capacity.ts`, `load-day-availability.ts` and the web `availability-reader.adapter.ts:238,304,395` parsing the old bodies — /book shows every shop closed; an appointments flip without clients would leave `recompute-client-stats.ts` parsing appointments through `appointmentFromDocument` (`:16`), breaking `dispatchClientProjections` and `seed:dev` (`load-domain.mjs:73` bundles it), a gate of that very flip; and `cancelAppointment`/`editAppointment` read `giftVouchers` and `couponGrants` in their transaction (`giftVoucherFromDocument`, `voucher-restore.ts:54`, `firestore-voucher-ledger.ts:27`) while `transitionAppointment` writes `auditLog` rows. The flips are therefore the **connected components of the reader matrix**, in this order: (0) the two-form `provideLazyPort` seam of §5.3 with its wiring spec, before the first web bundle; (1) **booking core** — `services`, `serviceCategories`, `barbers`, `locations`, `barberSchedules`, `scheduleExceptions`, `appointments`, `barberBusy`, `capacity`, `appointmentNotes`, `appointmentPhotos`, `waitlistRequests`, `notifications` (with its `hasOnly(['readAtMs'])` rule line, §3.5), `barberLeadTimeSamples`, `coupons`, `couponGrants` (with its `allow update: if false`, §3.5), `giftVouchers`, `auditLog`, `clientStats` + `restricted/money`, `backfillJobs` and the e2e `appointment-seed-document.ts` — with **every** handler, adapter and seed path that reads or writes those bodies: `FirestoreBookingStore`, `rebuild-busy`, `rebuild-capacity`, `load-day-availability`, `sample-lead-time`, the waitlist store and matcher, `voucher-restore`/`firestore-voucher-ledger`, `firestore-discount-resolver`, `recompute-client-stats.ts` → `projectClientStats` with `dispatchClientProjections` and the three policy-recompute entry points, `run-backfill` (both jobs — the subjectMirror job reads appointments and the commit audit rows), the `auditProfileChanges` trigger's audit-row write and the streak-definition store's audit-row write (both moved onto `firestore-audit.adapter.ts`; the rest of that store waits for flip 3), the `load-domain.mjs` seed path (rewritten to bundle `project-client-stats.pipeline`) and the web bundles of all of them; (2) **identity and accounts** — `users`, `otps` (with all twelve `libs/domain/models` importers, §1.4), `impersonationSessions`; (3) **loyalty and invitations** — `invitations`, `loyaltyAccounts`, `clientJournal`, `streakDefinitions` + versions, the badge/season/tier/rewards catalogue; (4) **programs** — `positions`, `courses`, `events`. (`settings/bookingPolicy` keeps its body, §2.6, and flips nothing.) Flip (1) is large by necessity: today's booking transaction reads the catalog, the roster, appointments, vouchers and grants at once, so no producer-before-consumer re-ordering can split it. **The reader matrix** is written in 3a as the first table of `docs/architecture/firestore-runbook.md`, from a grep of every collection constant and literal: for each collection, every server handler, server adapter, web adapter, store and seed path that reads it (e.g. `locations`: `FirestoreBookingStore.load` `toShop`, `rebuild-capacity.ts`, `load-day-availability.ts`, `availability-reader.adapter.ts`, `catalog-reader.adapter.ts:209-224`, the seed; `giftVouchers`: `voucher-restore.ts`, `firestore-voucher-ledger.ts`, `client-vouchers-reader.adapter.ts`, `gift-voucher-reader.adapter.ts`, the seed; `appointments`: every booking handler, `recompute-client-stats.ts`, `run-backfill.ts`, `client-history-reader.adapter.ts`, `appointment-repository.adapter.ts`, `load-domain.mjs`, the e2e seed); the closure above is its result on 2026-10-10, re-derived before each flip. **Per-flip grep gate:** after the flip, no surviving `apps/functions/src/lib/**`, `apps/functions/src/adapters/**`, `libs/infrastructure/**` adapter, web store or `tools/seed/**`/`tools/seed-dev-catalog.mjs` file names a field the flip removed (`timeSlot`, `startIso`, `hours`, `timezone`, `weeklyPattern`, a root `priceMinorUnits`, `balanceMinorUnits`, `lifetimeSpendMinor`, coupons' `enabled`, `startDateIso`, `*AtIso`, …). **Each flip carries, in one commit:** its collections' pipelines and server adapters, **every surviving reader of them** (the matrix), their web `*.adapter.ts` bundles and the `app.config.ts` rebinding of their tokens (rows moved from `adapter` to `factory`, §5.3), **every `new XxxUseCase` site and every component injecting a token the flip rebinds** — enumerated per flip from a grep of the token names (flip (1) alone: `new ObserveRangeCapacityUseCase(this.availability)` at `booking-schedule-step.ts:168`, `new ListServicesGroupedByCategoryUseCase(this.catalog)` at `admin-rhythm.ts:479`, the three `ObserveUpcomingUseCase` and two `ObserveDayAvailabilityUseCase` sites, `CancelAppointmentUseCase`; flip (2): `new UpdateProfileUseCase(inject(PROFILE_PORT))` at `profile.store.ts:37` and `onboarding-flow.store.ts:78` — `PROFILE_PORT` is a `provideLazyPort` row over the `users` body (`app.config.ts:465`), so the users flip rebinds it; flip (3): `new ObserveStreakDefinitionUseCase(this.definitions)` and `new PublishStreakDefinitionUseCase(this.definitions)` over `STREAK_DEFINITION_REPOSITORY` at `admin-rhythm.store.ts:585,589`; flip (4): the ten `admin-programs.store.ts:89-120` sites over `POSITION_REPOSITORY`/`COURSE_REPOSITORY`/`SHOP_EVENT_REPOSITORY` — `ObserveAllPositionsUseCase`, `ObserveAllCoursesUseCase`, `ObserveUpcomingShopEventsUseCase`, `ObservePastShopEventsUseCase`, `CreatePositionUseCase`, `UpdatePositionUseCase`, `CreateCourseUseCase`, `UpdateCourseUseCase`, `CreateShopEventUseCase`, `UpdateShopEventUseCase` — and the four marketing sites, `ObserveOpenPositionsUseCase` (`marketing-careers.ts:85`), `ObserveCoursesUseCase` (`marketing-courses.ts:85`), `ObserveUpcomingShopEventsUseCase`/`ObservePastShopEventsUseCase` (`marketing-events.ts:74-75`)), the store fields that consume them re-typed to the entities (§5.1), their shape-driven `firestore.rules` lines and rules-spec cases, their `firestore.indexes.json` composites and fieldOverrides (§3.3, §3.4), their `tools/seed/fixtures/*.ts` bodies — and it deletes those collections' old use-cases, server adapters, `lib/**` handler code and web class adapters (by the deletion rule below). Phase 4 then deletes only the use-cases whose tokens no flip touched — the ones over tokens bound to no collection body: `EnsureSessionReadyUseCase`/`SignOutUseCase` over `AUTH_GATEWAY` (`session.ts:16`, `site-menu.component.ts:101`, `onboarding-flow.store.ts:74,77`), `RequestOtpUseCase`/`VerifyOtpUseCase`/`RegisterUserUseCase` over `OTP_CLIENT` (`auth-flow.store.ts:49,52`, `onboarding-flow.store.ts:71`; both tokens are eager `useClass` callable/Auth clients, `app.config.ts:267-268`, which the identity flip does not rebind), `UploadAvatarUseCase`/`RemoveAvatarUseCase` over the Storage-backed `AVATAR_UPLOADER` (`profile.store.ts:40,43`, `onboarding-flow.store.ts:81`) and `PreviewStreakDefinitionUseCase`, which takes no port (`admin-rhythm.preview.ts:161`); programs and streak definitions are not among them — flips (4) and (3) rebind their tokens and move their sites. **Every reader of a collection therefore matches its shape at every commit** (no dual shapes, CLAUDE.md §0), each flip is reviewable alone, and each is gated by `e2e:web` (below).

The §4.2 browser-side command pipelines (the read-then-rebuild landings of §5.1) live beside the feature store that uses them; the shared `callableClient` stays in `libs/infrastructure/*` beside the adapters; there is no `libs/web-pipelines` lib. The pipeline specs and the `@creativo/ecs-core/testing` doubles do not depend on the folder. the use-case unit specs map as `commit-booking.use-case.spec.ts` → `book-appointment.pipeline.spec.ts`, `staff-edit-appointment.undo.spec.ts` → `edit-appointment.pipeline.spec.ts` (booking-core flip), `request-otp`/`verify-otp`/`complete-registration.use-case.spec.ts` → `request-otp`/`verify-otp`/`complete-registration.pipeline.spec.ts` (identity flip), `publish-streak-definition.use-case.spec.ts` → `publish-streak-definition.pipeline.spec.ts` (loyalty flip; its refusal cases already in `streak-publish.system.spec.ts`, Phase 2); `firestore.rules.integration.spec.ts` extended in each flip for its shape-driven renames only (the tightening cases arrive with their Phase 4 commits); `appointment-seed-document.ts` (e2e) rewritten to the ms body in the booking-core flip with its `satisfies`; the seven `tools/seed/*.spec.mjs` re-targeted per §7; the emulator spec gains the reopen-vs-commit race (`transitionAppointment`), the grant burn/restore cases (`editAppointment`, `cancelAppointment`) and the duplicate-trigger case of `matchWaitlist` (§4.1).

Gate (3a): `pnpm run verify:p0` (5 checks, (e) in owner-write mode) green against the new `main.ts`; `pnpm run test:emulator` green (every callable's emulator integration spec, `rebuild-capacity.integration.spec.ts` asserting the replace-not-merge invariant of §3.6 against today's map); `pnpm run seed:dev` against a wiped emulator (the seed still bundles `recompute-client-stats` by path); **`pnpm run e2e:web`** — 3a rewrites all 29 exports behind a new `main.ts`, and `verify:p0` does not exercise `/book`, the staff day or the client card. Gate (each 3b flip): all of the above plus the per-flip grep gate (no surviving reader names a removed field), `pnpm nx typecheck seed-tools` (the `satisfies` of every seeded body of the flipped collections against its entity) and a `pnpm run dev` smoke of the surfaces that read the flipped collections (`/book`, the staff day, the inbox, the client card as they flip) — the SPA must read its own database at every flip, and no build or unit gate can see that. Gate (end of 3b, after the last flip): `pnpm nx graph --file=graph.json` shows no `functions → libs/application/*` edge — spec and test-support edges included — **and**, as the assertion that actually proves the bundle claim, `dist/apps/functions/package.json` (`generatePackageJson`) lists no `@angular/*` or `rxjs`, checked by the `verify-p0.mjs` baseline check (added in Phase 1, re-recorded here); both move here from the old 3a gate because the `lib/**` handlers keep their `libs/application` imports until their own flip.

### Phase 4 — Client integration and legacy deletion

**Prerequisites: D6 — confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-10 (§9)** (this phase deletes `docs/architecture/domain-model.md` and banners `docs/migration-blueprint.md` under D6); D8, which decides whether `libs/domain/models` is deleted here, was already confirmed for Phase 1. The two-form `provideLazyPort` seam that used to open this phase is now flip (0) of Phase 3b (§5.3), because every web bundle lands in its flip.

- **Rules tightenings, one per web switch** (Risk 11, §3.5): each of the **three** remaining tightenings ships in the commit of the surface it closes — `impersonation.adapter.ts` → `startImpersonation`/`endImpersonation` callables + `impersonationSessions` write false; the invitation `+1` → `redeemInvitation` + the invitations closes; `BookingContactSheet.saveProfile` → `updateProfile` + `users/{uid}` client `allow update: if false` (the owner allowlist removed whole; a spec case asserts an owner `firstName` write is denied; `verify:p0` (e) switches to callable-only mode in that commit) — each with its own case in `firestore.rules.integration.spec.ts`. The `couponGrants` update false already shipped with the booking-core flip (its only client writer has no production caller, §3.1); here only the dead `FirestoreCouponGrantRepository.save`/`ApplyDiscountsUseCase` code is deleted. (The notifications `hasOnly(['readAtMs'])` line is a rename that shipped with the booking-core flip of Phase 3b, §3.5.) **The D9(a) delta:** a fourth tightening — positions/courses/events client writes → `false`, with its rules-spec case — ships in the commit that switches `AdminProgramsStore` to `saveProgramContent`.
- What the flips left in `libs/infrastructure/firestore`: `firestore.adapters.ts` / `firestore.lazy.ts` export only the bundle map (43 classes → ~25 bundles over the shared `observeCollection`/`observeDoc` helpers, written flip by flip); `libs/infrastructure/firebase-app/src/lib/ports.tokens.ts` holds the `InjectionToken<PortBundle>` constants; `translateDomainError` takes `{ code }`; under §9 D12(b) `contact-change.adapter.ts` + `contact-change.adapter.spec.ts` (and the barrel line `index.ts:12`) are deleted with the `CONTACT_CHANGE_PORT` / `CallableContactChangeAdapter` binding in `app.config.ts:71,101,271` — no successor, no callables.
- The rest of §5.1 — the store **fields** were re-typed in each collection's flip; here the derivations move into `computed()`s over systems: `StaffDayStore` rows become a `computed`; `BookingFlowStore` uses `BookingCartSystem` and derives day availability from the raw scheduling streams (§4.2); `BookingContactSheet`, impersonation and invitation writes move to callables; `AdminProgramsStore` stays a rules-guarded admin write under the recommended D9(b) (a `saveProgramContent` callable only under D9(a)).
- Deletions (shared, moved here from Phase 3): `libs/application/*` entirely (151 files; the rest of its `testing.ts` fixtures moved to `@creativo/ecs-core/testing` — the scheduling contract, the streak/loyalty fixtures and the two loyalty JSON files already moved in 3a: in-memory readers become port function doubles — `InMemoryNotificationReader` included, off the production barrel (tests Q7) — the deep-frozen loyalty JSON stays, `deepFreeze` moves with it); the ten application mapper specs die with the mappers once their rule cases were copied to system specs (Phase 2, §7); the behavioural `libs/application` specs die only after their §7 successors are green; `libs/domain/{identity,accounts,governance,notifications,programs,catalog,engagement,scheduling}` and, under D3(a), `kernel` — the kernel `Result` and its `Success`/`Failure` classes go here with the per-lib codemod of Risk 3 and the Phase 2 shim bridges — each deleted once `pnpm nx graph --file` shows no edge into it **and** every spec file of that lib has its §7 successor green or is marked dead with its legacy class (the non-scheduling domain spec row of §7) — the graph alone would let a rule vanish silently; the `new XxxUseCase` sites no flip touched (§6 Phase 3b's list: `EnsureSessionReadyUseCase`/`SignOutUseCase` over `AUTH_GATEWAY`, `RequestOtpUseCase`/`VerifyOtpUseCase`/`RegisterUserUseCase` over `OTP_CLIENT`, `UploadAvatarUseCase`/`RemoveAvatarUseCase` over `AVATAR_UPLOADER`, the port-less `PreviewStreakDefinitionUseCase` — programs, streak-definition and profile sites already went with flips (4), (3) and (2)), the four grid builders, the duplicated day-key/`dayKeyOf`/`countsToward` code, the undecorated helper classes, `libs/domain/models` (last lib), `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`; `module-boundaries.md` rewritten from the new graph; `docs/migration-blueprint.md` gets a superseded banner on the listed sections (D6). Under §9 D12(b) the contact-change slice goes with **no successor**: `libs/application/accounts/src/lib/ports/{contact-change.port,contact-change.errors,contact-change-target}.ts` and `use-cases/confirm-contact-change.{use-case,errors,use-case.spec}.ts` (barrel lines `index.ts:2,5,6,11,12`) with `libs/application/*`, and the feature comments that promise the callables (`booking-contact-sheet.ts:61`, `client-profile.html:193-197`) reworded in the same commit. **Packages:** in the commit that deletes the kernel — its `money.ts`, `zoned-date-time.ts`, `money.spec.ts` and `format-money.spec.ts` are the last importers — `dinero.js`, `luxon` and `@types/luxon` leave `package.json` (`:107`, `:115`, `:58`), together with the spec-only dinero property test in `libs/ecs-core/src/components/money.data.spec.ts` and its `no-restricted-imports` override in `libs/ecs-core/eslint.config.mjs` (§9 D4, D5); `libphonenumber-js` stays, imported only by `phone.system.ts`.
- **Re-point table for consumers outside the listed groups** (each deletion above is blocked until its row is done): (a) `libs/ui/controls/src/lib/phone-field/phone-field.ts:20,36,311` — static types `CountryIso2`/`PhoneDraft` and a **lazy** `import('@creativo/domain/kernel')` for the libphonenumber cage; it cannot become `import('@creativo/ecs-core')` without dragging the whole barrel into the chunk (`verify:bundle`), so a **secondary entry `@creativo/ecs-core/phone`** (`tsconfig.base.json` alias + `libs/ecs-core/src/phone.ts`) exports only `PhoneSystem`/`PhoneNumber`/`E164`/`PhoneCountry`/`PhoneDraft`/`CountryIso2` (with `PhoneSystem.parseCountry`, the `toCountryIso2` successor, §2.5; (c) `apps/web/e2e/support/seed-firestore.ts:10` and `apps/web/e2e/client-card-glance.spec.ts:5` — `LoyaltyAccountFixture` from `@creativo/ecs-core/testing`; `apps/web/e2e/support/sign-in.ts:2` — `import type { UserRole } from '@creativo/domain/accounts'` becomes `Role` from `@creativo/ecs-core` (a rename at its use sites, not only an import); (d) the six non-spec `apps/web/src` files — `app/app.config.ts`, `app/app.routes.ts`, `app/guards/home.guard.ts`, `app/guards/roles.guard.ts`, `app/guards/session.ts`, `app/shell/session-expiry.service.ts` — to `Principal`/`Role`/`SessionAccessSystem` from `@creativo/ecs-core` (their specs follow); (h) `libs/ui/controls/src/lib/phone-field/phone-field.spec.ts` — `@creativo/ecs-core/phone`, with the component in (a); (i) `formatMoney` — its about fifteen feature importers (today through the `@creativo/application/{booking,catalog}` re-exports of the kernel's `format-money.ts`) re-point to `libs/infrastructure/i18n`'s `formatMoney(money: Money, locale)` with the cached `Intl.NumberFormat` (§2.5), before the kernel and the application libs go.
- Nx: the `eslint.config.mjs` depConstraints (`@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`, `:86` onward — `nx.json` carries no depConstraints, grep on 2026-10-10, so this file is the only place) — **only the `type:application` rows are removed** (`:159-173`) and the tag retired; the `type:feature` row becomes `feature|ui|infrastructure|util|domain`, `type:infrastructure → domain|infrastructure|util`, `type:domain → domain`, and the **`type:ui → ui|tokens|util|domain` (`:174`), `type:util` (`:205`) and `type:tokens` (`:209`) rows are kept**, as is the `type:tooling → tooling|util|domain` row 3a added for `seed-tools` (§6 Phase 3) — phone-field and icon-registry depend on the `type:ui → domain` edge; under D10(b) every `domain` in these rows reads `ecs` (§6 Phase 1). The root `eslint.config.mjs` gains the `**/*.adapter.ts` class-ban block, the `**/*.port.ts` block and the token guard in the same commit that deletes the 40 class adapters and `libs/application/*` with its 44 port files (Phase 1 kept all three project-scoped).

Specs: feature store specs keep their cases against entity fixtures from `@creativo/ecs-core/testing`; e2e suite: **three files, three imports** — `seed-firestore.ts` and `client-card-glance.spec.ts` (`LoyaltyAccountFixture`), `sign-in.ts` (`UserRole` → `Role`, renamed at its use sites) — no case changes; `verify:bundle` guards the initial chunk and the `@creativo/ecs-core/phone` lazy chunk.

Gate: all five commands (`pnpm nx run-many -t lint` now with the root-widened adapter and token guards); `pnpm run verify:bundle`; `pnpm run verify:p0` ((e) via `updateProfile` only, once `users/{uid}` client updates are `false`); `pnpm run test:emulator` (the rules spec for impersonation / invitations / couponGrants / users / notifications, one case per tightening); `pnpm run e2e:web` on the emulator; `pnpm nx graph` shows no `libs/domain/*` or `libs/application/*` project (kernel per D3); `package.json` lists no `dinero.js`, `luxon` or `@types/luxon` and `grep -rn "from 'luxon'\|from 'dinero.js'"` over `libs/` and `apps/` is empty (§9 D4, D5).

**What keeps the app running between phases:** Phase 1 adds code nothing outside ecs-core imports; Phase 2 moves math behind shims inside the existing classes (public API unchanged) and is gated by `e2e:web`; Phase 3a keeps every callable name, document id **and document shape** — the new `main.ts` still delegates to today's handlers — so the SPA's readers are untouched; each 3b flip rewrites one read/write closure end to end (pipelines, server adapters, **every surviving reader**, web bundles, consuming store fields, rules, indexes, seed fixtures) in one commit with a wipe-and-reseed of the emulator (there are no production users to carry over) and is gated by `e2e:web` plus a dev smoke, because a flip is the one boundary where every build is green while the SPA could be blind; Phase 4 derives the rest of §5.1 in `computed()`s, ships each rules tightening in the commit of its own web switch, and deletes the legacy libs once the graph shows no edge into them.

## 8. Risks

| #   | Risk                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Likelihood / impact | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | A composite that orders on `timeInterval.startMs` (or `createdAtMs`, `sentAtMs`, `takenAtMs`, `atMs`) excludes every document lacking the field; a dev project reseeded late, or an e2e seed document still carrying ISO, returns partial "my appointments" / history / cooldown / rate-limit sets | medium / medium     | no dual-read or dual-write (CLAUDE.md §0): shapes, rules and indexes ship in one change, the emulator and dev projects are wiped and reseeded; the e2e `appointment-seed-document.ts` and every seed fixture body (moved to `tools/seed/fixtures/*.ts` for exactly this, §6 Phase 3 — `satisfies` does not exist in the `.mjs` the seed is written in today) carry a `satisfies` check against the entity, run by `pnpm nx typecheck seed-tools`, so a stale shape fails typecheck, not a query                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 2   | `capacity/{YYYY-MM}` shape change breaks the public month calendar (read `allow read: if true`, `firestore.rules:433-439`) or regresses the per-path replace invariant                                                                                                                             | medium / high       | D7 decided before Phase 3; the month doc is rewritten by the reseed, not dual-written; `CapacitySystem.applyPlan` + `rebuild-capacity.integration.spec.ts` guard the replace-not-merge invariant (§3.6)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 3   | 2,666 spec `isSuccess` sites and 922 production sites — codemod drift                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | high / medium       | codemod is a script in `tools/verify`, run per lib; typecheck is the oracle (`Success`/`Failure` classes removed in the same commit)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 4   | `no-namespace` exception + suffix-based lint: a `*.data.ts` sneaks a class, or a system reaches for a date library (`luxon`) or `Date` instead of `ZonedTimeSystem`'s table                                                                                                                        | medium / medium     | `tools/lint-rules/ecs-syntax.mjs` with its own spec; `pnpm nx lint ecs-core` in the gate; `files` globs are suffix-only (`eslint.config.mjs:219-222`); `luxon` stays banned by the root `no-restricted-imports` with no ecs-core exemption at all (§9 D5: native `Intl`), and `new Date`/`Date.now` by the purity selectors                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

| 7   | Transaction contention: `editAppointment` now touches grants + vouchers + busy in one tx                                                                                                                                                                                                           | low / medium        | vouchers and busy are the same scope as today's `FirestoreBookingStore` + settle calls; **grants are a new in-tx read + write** (today's `FirestoreDiscountResolver.grant` reads outside the tx and nothing server-side writes `couponGrants`, §4.1), so the conflict set grows by one document per grant named — the price of closing the double-burn race; each grant write is a CAS on the read `state` through `CouponGrantSystem.burn` (single-use → `used`, multi-use `remaining − 1`) and, for a grant discount a save removes or a cancel releases, `CouponGrantSystem.restore` — so the sheet's «Отмени» undo re-applies a grant instead of meeting `wrong_state` (§4.1 `editAppointment`/`cancelAppointment`); `operationDigest` makes retries idempotent; `retry: true` on triggers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 8   | Seed and e2e hand-written documents diverge from entity bodies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | high / low          | seed imports built systems and entity companions; `appointment-seed-document.ts` rewritten; the fixture bodies live in `tools/seed/fixtures/*.ts` with `satisfies Omit<XEntity, 'id'>` on every export and `seed-tools` gets a `typecheck` target (`.mjs` cannot carry `satisfies`, §6 Phase 3)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| D29 | Customer vs user — whether the shop's client record and the Firebase Auth account are one entity (Law 7.4: `CustomerId` and `UserId` strictly distinct, never one value used as both)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | (a) a `customers/{customerId}` collection: `customerId = CustomerId.forUser(uid)` (`cus_` + 20 hex of a hash of the uid) for an account holder, a random `cus_…` id for a walk-in, the account linked by an explicit nullable `Customer.userId`; the record created idempotently inside the transaction that first needs it (`tx.get` by a derivable path, no query); (b) `customers/{random}` for everyone, resolved by `where('userId', '==', uid)` — a query inside every booking transaction, and a race creates two records for one account unless a lock document is added; (c) keep the uid as the client key (status quo: `clientStats/{uid}`, `subjectUserIds`) — one value used as both, and a walk-in can never have stats, loyalty or photos | **Decided 2026-10-10 under the owner's locked CustomerId/UserId rule: (a)** (`docs/architecture/flatten-spec.md` §5). Who acted, who is notified or who may read a document → `UserId`; whom the shop served, billed or rewarded → `CustomerId`; a document that needs both carries both as two fields with two values. The flatten pass lands the vocabulary only — the `CustomerId` brand with `forUser`, the `Customer` entity and `CustomerOrigin`, `LoadCustomerForUser`, `Collections.Customers` — and every client reference keeps its `UserId` name and type; there is no uid→`CustomerId` conversion and no cast between the brands (lint). Each 3b flip lands its own collections: flip (1) adds the `CustomerId` fields with real `forUser` values (appointments `ownerCustomerId` + `subjectCustomerIds`, clientStats + money re-keyed, couponGrants, giftVouchers, appointmentPhotos, auditLog, backfill/policy jobs) beside explicit account-access fields that the rules key on (`ownerUserId` kept on appointments, `holderUserId` on grants and vouchers), the `customers` rules (staff read/write, owner read on `userId`), the FIRST_BOOKING creation path and the seed's customers; flip (2) adds the REGISTRATION path; flip (3) re-keys `loyaltyAccounts`, `clientJournal` and the progress subcollections. A staff walk-in with a name gets a customer record and no account; merging it with an account that registers later is D26's design-only merge (open) |
